correctness.rationale: Fourier slice and sine product recover the weighted-width multisets from complete sections; the three-cycle gives exactly equal products in every d≥3. The generic d=3 classification follows from examining all six permutations, excluding transpositions when ratios differ and factoring the 3-cycle elementary-symmetric difference; the inverse cycle reverses the same pair. Three explicit full-support normals have squared-component matrix determinant 1/12 and reconstruct squares of all three sides from variances. Symbolic factorization, rational permutation enumeration, products, and 3-view matrix inverse were checked by verify.py, independently of the all-dimensional reasoning.

originality.rationale: The central source arXiv:2610.10229v1 treats reconstruction from continuum-direction section data, not a finite fixed pair for labelled orthotopes. The closest published-finding corpus orthotope finding was inspected in full and instead reconstructs unordered sides from Haar-random projection-volume moments. Targeted published-finding corpus and web searches for two fixed sections, weighted-width switching, and box-spline equivalences located no claimed two-view three-cycle fiber classification. The novel contribution is a complete generic ambiguity locus, a universal all-dimensional two-view obstruction, and matching dimension-three three-view reconstruction, not Fourier-sinc factorization or Newton identities individually. Unindexed spline or tomography literature could contain an equivalence.
residual_risks: Full-text historical box-spline/two-marginal inverse literature was not exhaustively inspected; an equivalent permutation-switch classification could exist.

value.rationale: A natural geometric inverse problem asks how many full hyperplane-section profiles at prescribed fully oblique directions uniquely reconstruct an axis-labelled rectangular solid. The theorem establishes a sharp dimension-three threshold (two invariably insufficient, three explicitly sufficient), a complete parameterization of the exceptional two-view nonuniqueness locus when ratios are distinct, and equal-volume noncongruent counterexamples even with all offsets. These are structural and measurable statements, not just application of the sinc product.
